subject: Request: Downshift protections and staggered offboarding — CardiaMed approval needed
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: James Porter <james.porter@cardiamed.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Downshift protections and staggered offboarding — CardiaMed approval needed

Team,

Quick summary: CardiaMed (enterprise POC) is asking for an early-termination / staged downshift that includes a 90-day staggered ramp to 30% of committed capacity, an opt-out window at 60 days, and a credit bucket to blunt immediate revenue loss. They also want a one-time retroactive discount on the quarter of transition (they're asking ~35%). Procurement is pushing this through next-week since their board is reviewing spend.

Key asks from the customer (attached: ramp_schedule_v1.xlsx, draft_amendment.docx):
- 90-day staged ramp: 100% -> 70% (30 days) -> 50% (60 days) -> 30% (90 days)
- 60-day opt-out window to fully terminate without penalty if product doesn't meet KPIs
- Credit bucket to offset fees during transition (they propose $150k)
- One-time discount applied to the final active quarter during the ramp (they propose 35%)

Why we should consider: retention risk is high and this is a strategic healthcare account. If we walk on these asks without guardrails we expose ~$450k in ARR risk over next 6 months, but a structured protection may keep them as a scaled customer.

Requested: Exec approval for non-standard commercial terms (discount cap, credit bucket, and opt-out language) and permission to present a counterproposal that limits revenue exposure. I need a decision before EOD Friday so procurement can accept terms next week.

What I recommend as a starting point:
- Cap any one-time discount at 25% (not 35%)
- Credit bucket capped at $120k and drawn down monthly against invoices
- 90-day stagger is OK but require 60-day forecast updates and a 30-day notice before each step
- Opt-out language: allow termination with a 60-day notice but require forfeiture of any remaining credit bucket if termination occurs before day 90 (protects us)

Attachments: ramp_schedule_v1.xlsx, draft_amendment.docx

Please advise who can sign off or what limits we should hold to.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Downshift protections and staggered offboarding — CardiaMed approval needed

Marcus —

Thanks for the concise summary. High level: I support negotiating a structured downshift instead of a hard churn, but we need firm guardrails. Please do not agree to anything over 25% discount or a credit bucket > $120k without final approval from Finance. Also make sure we capture a contract amendment that:
- Limits the total exposure (cap language)
- Requires monthly usage forecasts during the ramp
- Includes a renewal trigger if usage returns above 60% within 180 days

Can you confirm the expected revenue impact (monthly burn) under your proposed schedule so Finance can run worst-case scenario? Loop in legal to get opt-out wording redlined. If we have buy-in from Legal and Finance by Thursday, I'll escalate to Lisa for final exec signoff if needed.

-Lauren
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Downshift protections and staggered offboarding — CardiaMed approval needed

Marcus / Lauren —

I reviewed the draft amendment. Legal is comfortable with a staged ramp but request these clarifications and edits (attached: ramp_amendment_redline.docx):

1) Discount cap: we should commit to a maximum one-time discount of 25% and prohibit stacking with any partner or marketplace credits.
2) Credit bucket: acceptable up to $120k, to be applied pro rata to invoices; any unused portion after 180 days reverts to Redwood. Customer forfeits remaining credit on any early termination before day 90 unless otherwise negotiated by execs.
3) Opt-out language: redline requires a 60-day termination notice and a customer-specified reason; we will include an SLA remediation process that must be initiated prior to opt-out. If remediation is unsuccessful, opt-out is allowed.
4) Forecasting: require rolling 60-day forecast every 30 days; failure to provide forecast allows us to pause non-critical features or throttle capacity after 14 days' notice.
5) Data/security carveouts: all data retention and audit obligations remain unchanged; the amendment must not change security SLAs or liability caps.

Please confirm CardiaMed is prepared to accept these changes. Marcus, once CardiaMed confirms, Legal needs an authorized signature name and finance will need the final amortization schedule.

Karthik
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Downshift protections and staggered offboarding — CardiaMed approval needed

Team —

Finance review complete. Conditional approval to proceed with the customer counter we discussed, subject to the following final limits and controls (I will not approve exceptions beyond these without CFO sign-off):

- Discount: hard cap 25% one-time on the transition quarter.
- Credit bucket: maximum $120,000; will be drawn monthly against invoices (no cash payout).
- Ramp schedule: 90-day staged ramp acceptable provided CardiaMed provides rolling 60-day forecasts every 30 days.
- Termination / opt-out: Customer may terminate with 60 days' notice after the SLA remediation window. If termination occurs before day 90 the remaining credit bucket is forfeited.
- Reporting & monitoring: Account team must log this amendment in HubSpot with the deal id (CARD-2026-3347) and create a renewal trigger ticket for CS to monitor usage recovery.

Next steps: Marcus, present the redlined amendment to CardiaMed and obtain a named signer. Legal will finalize the DocuSign packet once we have the exact signer and the customer accepts the redlines. I'll prepare the amortization schedule and the authorization_summary.pdf for executive records.

Monica Patel
Director, Finance — Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
